summary: Tower Point, Ochoco National Forest, Oregon: a lookout site since 1919, with the present 20-ft timber L-4 tower built 1955; registered 2022, unstaffed on a 2021 visit.

facts.design: 20-foot open treated timber tower with an L-4 cab
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Ochoco National Forest; Bureau of Land Management a cooperator

staffing.status: Staffed every summer per Rex's Forest Fire Lookout Page; unstaffed on a June 2021 visit

access.note: Reached by forest roads. On a June 2021 visit the catwalk hatch was latched shut and the cab could not be reached. Check with the Ochoco National Forest before visiting.

visit.trail_note: Forest roads 1750 and 1760 from Road 16 to the summit; a 2021 visitor found the road a bit rough but very doable and noted the last stretch had no gate.

A timber tower erected at the site
Present 20-foot treated timber L-4 tower built

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1919 lookout, the 1940 timber tower and the 1955 L-4 tower are different structures on the same site; 1955 is the current tower. The Oregon listing's 1936 cab date is not repeated by the NHLR or by Rex's page, so it is recorded as uncorroborated.

Cheryl Hill's page is headed 'Staffed', yet the tower was unstaffed on her June 2021 visit. Rex's page says it is staffed every summer, so the tower appears to be seasonal rather than staffed year-round.

notes_for_editor: The 1936 cab date and the 1919 lookout detail come from a timeline on one lookout-history site, quoting old newspapers; the newspapers themselves were not read. The Ochoco National Forest history PDF (fs.usda.gov/media/260569) was scanned and does not name Tower Point. Current (2026) staffing and access are not confirmed; the 2021 visit is the newest first-hand account. The NHLR page lists a 2021 photo by Cheryl Hill but gives no photo URL, so no photo was added. Elevation is 6,090 ft in the NHLR and 6,086 ft on the other two sites; not used in facts.
